nodes.name: One-step electrodeposition of NiFe LDHs–NiFe alloy gradient hybrid on CC
nodes.procedure: In a typical procedure, a certain amount of FeSO4·7H2O was poured into 200 ml deionized (DI) water containing 228.4 mmol NiSO4·6H2O, 33.7 mmol NiCl2·6H2O, 129.4 mmol H3BO3 and 0.14 mmol C12H25NaO4S to obtain the electrodeposition bath solution (Fe²⁺/Ni²⁺ molar ratio of 0.40:1 for NF10). KOH-treated CC (1 cm × 3 cm, W0S1009) acted as cathode against two parallel graphite plates. Electrodeposition performed at current density 0.33 A·cm⁻², temperature (50.0 ± 0.1) °C for 90 s, resulting in in situ growth of NiFe LDHs–NiFe alloy gradient hybrid coating.

nodes.characterization_summary: NF10 electrode shows diffraction peak at 2θ ~11.7° indexed to (003) lattice plane of NiFe LDHs, NiFe alloy phases, and low crystallinity with 80.8 wt% NiFe alloy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably, the diffraction peak centered at 2θ of ∼11.7°, indexed to (003) lattice plane of NiFe LDHs [33, 34], emerges after Fe2+/Ni2+ molar ratio exceeds 0.20:1 (Fig. 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: NF10 electrode shows interconnected O-rich nanosheets on top surface with Fe/Ni molar ratio ~1:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS spot analyses and top surface morphologies reveal that interconnected O-rich nanosheets grow on the NF10 electrode with an Fe/Ni molar ratio of approximately 1:1, as shown in Figs. S8, S9.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDHs nanosheets show heavily disordered lattice fringes, voids, and dim SAED diffraction rings indicating low-crystalline nature with numerous lattice defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM image in Fig. 1d shows heavily disordered lattice fringes or even voids (marked with red circles), together with the SAED pattern with very dim diffraction rings, providing evidence of numerous lattice defects in the NiFe LDHs nanosheets with a low-crystalline nature.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cross-section EDS line scan of NF10 shows O mainly on outer coating layer with gradient increase from inner to outer side; surface Fe/Ni ~1:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS line scan across the cross section of the NF10 electrode shows that the O is mainly located on the outer side of the coating layer and follows a gradually increasing trend from the inner to the outer side (Fig. 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: As-prepared NiFe LDHs show 23.7% surface oxygen vacancies; XPS confirms Fe/Ni ratio 0.65:1 pristine, decreasing to 0.40:1 after OER and 0.28:1 after HER with NiOOH/Fe3+ (OER) and Fe0/Ni0/Ni2+-O (HER) species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. S31, the Fe/Ni molar ratio decreased from 0.65:1 to 0.40:1 after the OER and to 0.28:1 after the HER... it demonstrates that up to 23.7% of surface oxygen vacancies exist on the as-prepared NiFe LDHs.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine NF10 shows NiFe LDHs features; after OER shows NiOO- group and high-valence species formation; after HER shows no discernible Raman activity indicating metallic coating.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra illustrated in Fig. 3b show the formation of the NiOO− group and the transition from low-valence to high-valence species after the OER... no discernible Raman activity was observed for the A-HER sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine NF10 NiFe LDHs shows n-type conduction; after OER transitions to p-type conduction characteristics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Mott–Schottky plots... demonstrated the typical n-type conduction characteristics of NiFe LDHs and the transition to p-type conduction characteristics after the OER (Fig. 3c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Gently descending mass-loss step confirms low-crystalline nature of NiFe LDHs decomposition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This is also proved by the gently descending mass-loss step ascribed to the decomposition of NiFe LDHs (Fig. S12).
